It exists so that the section 5 proof -- the three sources F7 and F6 refused for an instrument reason classify CORRECTLY once the instrument is fixed -- is a rerunnable command rather than a sentence.
capture: Read in a browser on 2026-09-07 and transcribed. NOT digest-verified across two machines: that practice is what a RECORD's text costs, and none of these is a record. The char count and sha256 below are of the text as stored here, so a later reader can tell a re-transcription from a drifting source.

examples.text: Capture par le roi sassanide Shapur Ier (240-270/72) de l’empereur romain Valérien (253-260). Les deux antagonistes se font face, le premier saisit son ennemi par le poignet, qui tente de se défendre de son glaive. Le dynaste sassanide porte une barbe courte mais épaisse, nouée au bout du menton. Sa tête est surmontée d’un globe décoré de lignes convergentes. Les fanons de son diadème et les bouts de sa ceinture voltigent derrière lui. L’empereur romain, alors âgé de 67 ans, offre un visage juvénile et imberbe. Il est lauré et cuirassé, le paludamentum flottant dans son dos.

examples.what: parsigdatabase.com's own Persian statement that its 59 Manichaean Middle Persian texts, under Boyce 1975's sigla, carry a PERSIAN translation. NOT the M2 I or M 5794 I translation itself: those sit behind the site's search interface and were not captured in this session, and the negative is recorded rather than papered over. What this example proves is what FINDING 82 is about -- a non-English reference_translation -- and it proves it on real Persian prose from the source F6 was pointed at.
